packages.name: @base-ui/react
packages.reason: Base UI, the headless primitive layer the register is rebuilt on (issue #282, slice 2; issue text names it `@base-ui-components/react`, which npm has since renamed to `@base-ui/react` — the vendored shadcn source imports the new name). It owns focus, dismissal and ARIA for Dialog, Sheet, Menu, Tooltip, Tabs, Select and the Sidebar family, so behaviour the register's tests assert comes from one maintained implementation rather than a hand-rolled one.

packages.name: @earendil-works/pi-agent-core
packages.reason: Pi owns the agent loop (PRD decisions 13 and 31) and is adapted at the RunSession seam in slice 5.3. Pinned exactly so an upgrade is a reviewed change paired with the golden-corpus replay, never a silent lockfile move.

packages.name: @earendil-works/pi-ai
packages.reason: The message, model and stream types Pi's agent loop consumes and produces; the live launch's stream bridge builds an AssistantMessageEventStream with them (slice 6.11). It is the same build pi-agent-core depends on, pinned exactly so the bridge and the loop cannot drift apart across an implicit upgrade.

packages.name: @electron/packager
packages.reason: Builds the versioned desktop artifacts in the release pipeline (slice 11.7): it stages the app, the packaged web client and the prod dependency closure into the platform bundles the smoke test runs and the signed update manifest points at. Pinned exactly because the bundle layout — resources/app, the extra client resource and the executable name — is the release contract the smoke test asserts, so an implicit upgrade could move the artifact out from under a signed digest.

packages.name: @hono/node-server
packages.reason: The Node adapter between the API's fetch surface and node:http (slice 4.1). Pinned exactly because it owns how every request and response crosses that boundary, so an implicit upgrade is a change to request handling nobody reviewed.

packages.name: @orpc/client
packages.reason: The typed client and RPC link the contract's consumers call through (slice 4.1, PRD decisions 14 and 15). Pinned exactly because it owns the wire encoding on the client side; an implicit upgrade can change what a deployed client sends.

packages.name: @orpc/contract
packages.reason: The contract builder every procedure in packages/contracts is defined with (slice 4.1, PRD decisions 14 and 15). Pinned exactly because the contract is the single source of transport truth: a version move changes procedure, error and wire semantics for both client and server at once.

packages.name: @orpc/openapi
packages.reason: Generates the OpenAPI document from the same contract the router implements, asserted in the unit suite (slice 4.1, PRD decision 14). Pinned exactly because the generator decides the published document's shape, which is the promise the contract-first design makes.

packages.name: @orpc/server
packages.reason: Implements the contract, matches RPC requests and turns procedure errors into responses (slice 4.1, PRD decisions 14 and 28). Pinned exactly because it owns the server side of the wire protocol and the error envelope clients parse.

packages.name: @orpc/zod
packages.reason: Converts the contract's Zod schemas into JSON Schema for the OpenAPI document (slice 4.1). Pinned exactly because the conversion decides the document's schema output, and it must agree with the validation the same schemas perform at runtime.

packages.name: @phosphor-icons/react
packages.reason: The glyph set behind the register's `<Icon name>` facade (issue #282, slice 2). One pinned weight in `currentColor` keeps an icon from carrying a colour of its own, and a named glyph beats a pasted platform emoji (design record, Anti-goals).

packages.name: @playwright/test
packages.reason: Runs the release-critical browser tier against the built SPA and the offline API emulators (issue #96). Pinned exactly so browser protocol, tracing and screenshot behavior change only with a reviewed E2E update.

packages.name: @shadcn/lint
packages.reason: The design-system linter that replaces `ui-register.js` and `ui-colors.js` (issue #282, slice 0). Its rules name the fix, not just the fault — a restyling class is answered with the variant to use — which is what AGENTS.md's UI rules are re-pointed at.

packages.name: @tailwindcss/vite
packages.reason: The Vite plugin that compiles `apps/web/src/globals.css` into the built stylesheet (issue #282, slice 1). It is the same build as `tailwindcss`, pinned in step with it so the compiler and the plugin cannot drift apart across an implicit upgrade.

packages.name: better-auth
packages.reason: Email/password, sessions and verification for the one auth gate (slice 3.1, PRD decision 8). Pinned exactly because it owns password hashing, session-cookie issuance and origin checks, where an implicit upgrade is a security change nobody reviewed; the identity schema was generated for this library's table shape.

packages.name: class-variance-authority
packages.reason: The variant table the shadcn components declare their sizes and appearances with (issue #282, slice 2). `@shadcn/lint`'s no-restyle reads those tables to name the variant a caller should use instead of a restyling class, so the variant vocabulary and the lint guidance come from one declaration.

packages.name: clsx
packages.reason: The class joiner half of the register's `cn` helper (issue #282, slice 2). Conditional class lists are the one place a component composes classes, and this is the joiner the vendored shadcn source is written against.

packages.name: effect
packages.reason: The orchestration layer (PRD decision 12): provider services and their layers, retries, timeouts, resource safety, structured concurrency and typed error channels. Pinned exactly because its Cause, Layer and Context semantics are the error-mapping and lifetime contract every later service is written against; the major is chosen deliberately (3.x stable, not the 4.x release candidate).

packages.name: electron
packages.reason: The desktop shell itself (slice 11.6, PRD story 36): the process that hosts the packaged web build, the tray, native notifications and the signed-update check. Pinned exactly because the major decides the hardening defaults the desktop's call-site test asserts and the update artifact it accepts, so an implicit upgrade would move the sandbox, the context-isolation boundary and the release contract underfoot.

packages.name: graphile-worker
packages.reason: The durable job runner the worker boots (slice 6.1, PRD decision 17): job locking, retries and its own queue schema in Postgres. Pinned exactly because it migrates that schema at boot, so an implicit upgrade would silently change the queue's tables and job semantics on the production database.

packages.name: hono
packages.reason: The API's HTTP surface (slice 4.1, PRD decision 14: oRPC over Hono), mounted through the RPC handler and composed by every later route, stream and webhook. Pinned exactly because routing, middleware order and header handling are user-visible behaviors an implicit upgrade could move.

packages.name: sonner
packages.reason: The toast engine behind the register's `useToast` facade (issue #282, slice 2). Queueing, pause-on-hover and the live region are the parts a hand-rolled toast gets wrong, so they come from one maintained implementation while the call sites keep `push`/`dismiss`.

packages.name: tailwind-merge
packages.reason: The merge half of the register's `cn` helper (issue #282, slice 2): a later class in the same Tailwind group wins, so a caller's layout class cannot stack two paddings on top of a variant's. It is also the grammar `@shadcn/lint` classifies classes with when the project does not ship its own.

packages.name: tailwindcss
packages.reason: The CSS engine the UI stack is rebuilt on (issue #282, slice 1). It generates every utility class the shadcn register and the swept surfaces draw, and `@shadcn/lint`'s no-unknown-classes asks this build whether a class exists. Pinned exactly because the utility set is the design system's vocabulary: an implicit upgrade can add, rename or drop a class the register and the lint already rely on.

packages.name: varlock
packages.reason: The environment schema and audit CLI (varlock.dev) the root and per-package .env.schema files are written against, and the `env` CI tier runs. Pinned exactly because a schema is only a contract while the tool that reads it does not move underneath it: an upgrade can change decorator parsing, validation and `varlock audit` behavior at once.

packages.name: zod
packages.reason: The schema library every contract procedure is declared with and the one @orpc/zod converts into the OpenAPI document (slice 4.1, PRD decision 15). Pinned exactly because the same schemas validate requests at runtime and describe them publicly, so a move changes both validation behavior and the published document.

images.name: caddy
images.reason: The reverse proxy that terminates the one public origin (PRD decision 32, slice 12.2). Pinned by the digest its version tag was published under because it owns TLS termination, header forwarding and response flushing: a moving image would silently change whether token streaming works, and the integration suite drives this exact image against the shipped deploy/Caddyfile.

images.name: node
images.reason: The build and runtime base for every stage of the root Dockerfile except the backup's. The tag carries the exact Node version from .nvmrc, which pnpm's devEngines check refuses to substitute, and the digest keeps the stack on the image it was built and tested with.

images.name: node-trixie
images.reason: The backup image's base alone: the slim Node build of the same Debian release the pinned Postgres image runs, so the pg_dump and pg_restore copied into it (glibc trixie) load. The other services' bookworm base is one glibc older, and a glibc runs forwards, not backwards, so the server's clients cannot run there.

images.name: postgres
images.reason: The production major (PRD stack decision 11). The testkit harness boots it and the integration tier pulls it; the digest keeps both on the image the tier was proven against.
